references.name: Alvin Hansen, The American Economy
references.desc:
Data refuting the Fed's revisionist mythology about pre-1951
  inflationary policy; showed prices peaked before the Accord

references.name: Marriner Eccles, congressional testimony and letters
references.desc:
Fed Chairman who confirmed Fed stock conveys no ownership,
  reserves are created not deposited, and open market dealers function
  as a taxpayer-funded tollgate

references.name: Milton Friedman, The Federal Reserve After 50 Years
references.desc:
Conservative economist who agreed with Patman that unaccountable
  monetary authority is constitutionally and democratically indefensible

references.name: Paul Samuelson, The Federal Reserve After 50 Years
references.desc:
Liberal economist who agreed a central bank "not responsible is
  irresponsible rather than independent"

references.name: Robert V. Roosa, NY Fed testimony
references.desc:
Confirmed banks do not give the Fed cash deposits; reserves are
  bookkeeping credits created by the Fed

references.name: ABA, Money and Banking
references.desc:
Banking industry textbook that claimed "member banks own the
  12 Federal Reserve banks" — disputed by the Fed's own chairmen

references.name: Raymond P. Kent, Money and Banking
references.desc:
Academic text acknowledging FDIC examiners judge loan quality
  on repayment probability, not public welfare

references.name: Seymour E. Harris (Harvard), preface to A Primer on Money
references.desc:
Distinguished economist who endorsed Patman's analysis while
  noting his tendency to overstate; described banking opponents as
  "powerful, numerous, and well organized"

references.name: Employment Act of 1946
references.desc:
Congressional mandate for "maximum employment, production, and
  purchasing power" — Patman argues the Fed was supposed to serve this
  mandate but systematically ignored it

references.name: Pujo Committee Investigation
references.desc:
Exposed the "money trust" — Wall Street holding companies and
  interlocking directorates controlling most major U.S. banks; provided
  the public pressure for a public central bank
